patients.summary: Young man who joined as a healthy university student in 2020, developed schizophrenia in 2022 and was found to have the neuromuscular form of glycogen storage disease type IV. An MDMA intoxication with rhabdomyolysis and two episodes of neuroleptic malignant syndrome followed; he is now on clozapine under psychiatry with lab monitoring drawn at the practice.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Calvin called, age 20, wants a primary care doctor here. Had been seeing a pediatric office until he aged out. Covered on his parents' plan, card info entered. Heading back to campus later in September, so he'd like to be seen before then. Booked new patient physical 9/1 at 9:00. Records release for the pediatric office emailed to him to sign.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o man establishing care. Aged out of his pediatrician. Starting his third year at the university, lives with his parents when home, which is most of the time right now since classes are partly remote.

Feels well. No complaints today. No regular medicines, no supplements. NKDA.

PMH: nothing chronic. PSH: tonsils out at age 8, no anesthesia problems he knows of.
FH: he says his mother has a mental health condition and is followed by a psychiatrist; he did not want to go into detail and I did not push. Paternal grandfather had a drinking problem. Nothing cardiac or cancer that he knows of.
SH: never smoked, no vaping. Doesn't drink. No drugs. Not sexually active currently. Walks a lot on campus.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: Pleasant, good eye contact, well groomed. HEENT normal, tonsillar pillars surgically absent. Neck supple, no nodes, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin clear. Extremities normal, full strength. Neuro grossly intact.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P: healthy young adult.
- One-time HIV and hep C screening, and baseline CBC/CMP since he's never had blood work as an adult.
- Requesting pediatric records for immunizations.
- Flu shot when the fall supply arrives; nurse visit.
- Annual visit next summer.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Calvin, all of your blood work from Tuesday is normal, including the HIV and hepatitis C screens. Nothing to do. Good luck with the semester.

documents.title: Records from prior pediatric practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pediatric records received by fax, 34 pages, scanned.

Summary for the chart:
- Tonsillectomy at age 8 for recurrent tonsillitis, uncomplicated.
- Well visits yearly through age 18, growth normal.
- Childhood series complete. Adolescent vaccines on file: Tdap at 11, MenACWY at 11 and 16, HPV 2-dose series at 12.
- No chronic diagnoses, no medications, no allergies listed.

Immunization history updated. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal flu vaccine. Afebrile, no illness today, no prior reactions. VIS given. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated, observed 15 min, left without issue.

documents.title: Covid vaccine card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I got both Pfizer shots at the pharmacy downtown, April 20 and May 11. Photo of the card is attached. School wants proof from my doctor's office too, can you put it in my record?

documents.title: RE: Covid vaccine card
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Calvin, both doses are entered in your immunization record now. You can print the immunization summary from the portal under Health Summary for the school.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Going back in person for the fall term, says the remote year was dull but grades fine. No health concerns.

Meds none. NKDA. Still no tobacco, no alcohol. Sleeping ok.

Exam: well appearing, BP and weight as charted, unchanged from last year. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. Full strength throughout.

PHQ-2 0.

Plan: one-time lipid panel. Covid series complete. Flu shot in October. Td not due until his early thirties. See next summer.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given, right deltoid, 0.5 mL IM. Home for a long weekend. No illness, no egg or vaccine reactions. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Outside vaccine report
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State registry query shows a Pfizer booster given 1/14/22 at a community pharmacy. Added to immunization history.

documents.title: Appointment reminder
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Calvin, this is a reminder that your yearly physical is booked for Tuesday August 9 at 10:30. Reply here or call if you need to move it.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not come to physical yesterday. Called cell, no answer, mailbox full. Portal message sent asking him to call and reschedule.

documents.title: Call from patient's mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Mother called, very worried about Calvin. Pt has a signed release on file allowing us to speak with his parents (signed at new patient visit).

She says since the spring he has been pulling away from everyone. Did not go back to school in August, told them he was done with it. Stays in his room most of the day, she hears him talking quietly when no one is there. Lately says things about the family watching him. Not showering, wearing the same clothes. Eating very little. No statements about hurting himself or anyone else per mother, no weapons in the home. No known drug use but she isn't sure.

He has agreed to come in if she drives him. Booked with PCP Monday 10/17 at 2:00, double slot. Told her to call 911 or go to the ED if he talks about harming himself or others or becomes unsafe. She verbalized understanding. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read. Agree with Monday. I will plan to see him partly with mother and partly alone.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his mother for the first part of the visit, then alone.

Mother's account: over roughly the last six months he has withdrawn from friends and from the family. Left the university in August without finishing the term registration. Spends most of the day in his room. Barely eats with them. Stopped showering regularly. Recently accused them of watching him. She hears him murmuring to himself at night.

Alone, Calvin is guarded. Says he left school because "it wasn't safe to stay there" and would not say more. Asked if he hears voices, he paused a long time and said "not like you think." Denies wanting to hurt himself or anyone. Denies drugs and alcohol. Says he sleeps "in pieces." Not interested in eating much. Agrees his weight is down.

Exam: thin, unshaven, clothes worn several days. Vitals as charted, afebrile. Weight 69.5 kg, down about 10 lb from last year. Affect flat, eye contact poor, answers brief and at times trail off. No tremor, no rigidity, gait normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart and lungs normal. No focal neuro findings.

PHQ-9 6, mostly sleep, appetite and concentration items; item 9 zero.

A/P: months of social withdrawal, suspiciousness, decline in self-care and probable perceptual disturbance in a 22 y/o with a family history of serious mental illness. Concern for a primary psychotic disorder. Not acutely unsafe today, mother present at home, both aware of ED and 988.
- Medical screen today: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, urine drug screen.
- Urgent psychiatry referral placed; front desk to call the intake line today. Mother will drive him.
- Recheck weight in a few weeks.
- I will call mother once intake is set.

documents.title: Referral to Psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Urgent referral. 22 y/o man, about six months of social withdrawal, paranoid ideas about family surveillance, poor self-care, weight loss of about 10 lb, probable auditory perceptual disturbance; left university in August. No prior psychiatric care. Denies SI/HI today. No medications, NKDA. Medical screening labs sent today, will forward. Family history of psychiatric illness on mother's side. Patient agrees to be seen; mother will accompany.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calvin, your blood counts, chemistry, thyroid, B12 and urine screen all came back normal. I've sent them to the psychiatry office. Your intake there is on the 28th; the front desk confirmed with your mom. Call me anytime before then.

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Diagnostic Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY, COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC
Date of evaluation: 10/28/2022
Referred by: primary care

Identifying data: 22-year-old single man, lives with his parents, accompanied by his mother. First contact with any mental health provider.

Presenting problem: Over the past several months the family has watched him become steadily stranger in his behavior. He left university two months ago. He now keeps to his bedroom nearly all day and his mother hears him whispering there when he is alone. He refuses to come to family meals. He has told his parents that they hid cameras inside the walls, and he believes government agents follow his phone. He no longer bathes or changes his clothes. His speech has become hard to follow. He eats very little, has lost about 10 pounds and rarely leaves the house. He minimizes all of this.

Past psychiatric history: none. No prior hospitalization, no prior medication trials, no suicide attempts.
Substances: denies alcohol, cannabis and other drugs. Never smoked. Recent urine screen from primary care negative.
Medical: no chronic illness. Tonsillectomy in childhood. No current medications. NKDA.
Family: mother has schizophrenia and is in treatment. A maternal uncle has a long-standing psychiatric illness. Paternal grandfather with alcohol use disorder.
Social: unemployed since leaving school; lives with parents; on parents' insurance.

Mental status: disheveled young man, poor hygiene. Inattentive throughout; muttering under his breath; repeatedly glances up toward the ceiling while questions are asked. Speech soft, tangential at times. Mood "fine." Affect blunted. Thought content with persecutory delusions about surveillance by family and government. Endorses hearing whispering; does not describe command content. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. Insight poor, judgment fair (came in, accepts follow-up).

Assessment: Psychotic symptoms with functional decline for well over six months including the prodromal withdrawal, without a prominent mood episode or substance cause and with a normal medical screen. Diagnosis: schizophrenia.

Plan:
1. Recommended starting an antipsychotic and reviewed benefits and side effects with him and his mother. He declined, stating he does not trust medicines. Not committable today; no imminent risk.
2. Weekly to biweekly visits with this clinic, case management referral, family psychoeducation for parents.
3. Crisis plan reviewed with mother.
4. Will revisit medication at each visit.

Thank you for the referral.
Attending psychiatrist

documents.title: Call with mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called mother after reading the psychiatry evaluation. They have a second visit this week. He has refused medication so far. She is going to the family education group. Eating a little better. No safety concerns. Schizophrenia added to problem list. Asked her to have him come in for a weight check before the new year.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, follow-up summary to primary care. Visit 12/6/2022.

Calvin has attended four of five scheduled visits since intake. Still hears whispering and still believes his phone is monitored, but he is talking more in sessions and showered before today's visit. Eating with his parents a few nights a week. Continues to decline antipsychotic medication; we discussed it again today. No suicidal ideation. Case manager assigned.

Dx: schizophrenia. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: visits every two weeks, ongoing medication discussion, family group for parents.

events.reason: Muscle cramps with exertion, dark urine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: exertional cramps with pigmenturia, elevated CK

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in alone today for the weight check, and brought up something new: muscle cramping.

HPI: 23 y/o with schizophrenia (followed by community psychiatry, no meds). He says ever since high school, any short hard effort, like sprinting or lifting weights, brings on bad cramps in his thighs and arms and he has to stop. They ease within a few minutes of resting. A few times a year the next morning his urine has been dark, like cola. Walking, even for hours, is no problem. He started doing push-ups and squats in his room last week and had cramping, then dark urine yesterday morning; he collected this morning's first void in a cup we gave him. No injury, no joint pain, no rash, no fever. He says his father had something similar, got cramps and brown urine during military training. Denies alcohol and drugs. No medications.

Psych: more engaged than in October, answers fully, still somewhat guarded. Denies SI.

Exam: weight 70 kg. Vitals normal. No muscle tenderness. Bulk normal, no atrophy. Strength 5/5 proximally and distally in arms and legs. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Gait normal. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs today: CK 640 (high). UA from this morning: dipstick moderate blood, microscopy 0 RBC. Creatinine and potassium normal.

A/P:
1. Exertional cramps since adolescence with episodic pigmenturia, heme-positive urine without red cells, and an elevated resting CK, normal exam between episodes. Picture of a metabolic myopathy, glycogen storage type most likely. Referral to the neuromuscular clinic for evaluation and genetic testing. Until then: avoid short all-out efforts and heavy lifting, stay hydrated, and if urine turns dark again with pain or he feels unwell, go to the ED.
2. Schizophrenia: per psychiatry. Weight up a little.
3. Flu vaccine offered, declined today.

documents.title: Your results and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calvin, as we discussed, the muscle enzyme (CK) was 640, above the normal range, and the urine test picked up pigment without blood cells, which fits muscle breakdown after exercise. Your kidney numbers are normal. The neuromuscular clinic referral is in; their scheduler will call you. Easy on the push-ups until then.

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC, DEPARTMENT OF NEUROLOGY
Consultation, 2/21/2023. Requested by primary care.

Reason: exertional myalgia and cramps with episodes of dark urine.

History: 23-year-old man with symptoms since about age 15. Brief high-intensity effort (sprints, weight sets) produces painful cramping of the thighs and arms within a minute or two, relieved by a few minutes of rest. Several times, cola-colored urine the following morning. Sustained low-level exercise is tolerated. No fixed weakness, no dysphagia, no breathing difficulty, no palpitations. No jaundice or abdominal swelling ever. Never hospitalized for these episodes.

PMH: schizophrenia, followed by community psychiatry, no medications. Tonsillectomy in childhood.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: no known neuromuscular disease; patient relays a story of his father having exertional cramps in the military, not evaluated. Mother with schizophrenia.
Social: lives with parents, not working or in school. Never smoker. No alcohol or drugs.

Exam: normal bulk, no fasciculations. Neck flexion, deltoids, biceps, triceps, hip flexors, quadriceps, hamstrings and ankle muscles 5/5. Reflexes symmetric. Sensation intact. No hepatosplenomegaly. Cardiac rhythm regular.

Data: PCP CK 640 and heme-positive urine without RBCs. CK today 610.

Impression: metabolic myopathy with exercise intolerance and recurrent myoglobinuria; a glycogen storage disorder is the leading consideration.

Plan:
- Next-generation sequencing panel for metabolic myopathies, sent today.
- Echocardiogram and abdominal ultrasound, given that some glycogen storage disorders involve the heart and liver.
- Activity guidance: avoid maximal short-burst effort; moderate aerobic activity is fine; hydrate; urgent care for dark urine with pain.
- Return after results.

Neuromuscular attending

reports.text: Indication: metabolic myopathy, screen for cardiac involvement. Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 60% by biplane method. Normal regional wall motion. Normal diastolic filling for age. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.

Indication: metabolic myopathy, screen for liver involvement. The liver measures 14.8 cm, normal echotexture, smooth contour, no focal lesion. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Gallbladder normal without stones. Common bile duct 3 mm. Pancreas unremarkable where seen. Spleen 10.2 cm, homogeneous. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal abdominal ultrasound. Normal liver and spleen.

documents.title: Imaging reports received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Echo and abdominal ultrasound reports from the hospital imaging department (ordered by neuromuscular clinic) received and attached. Routed to PCP.

conditions.label: Glycogen storage disease type IV (Andersen disease)

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Follow-up: Genetic Results
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Follow-up visit 4/11/2023.

Results: The metabolic myopathy panel identified two pathogenic variants in GBE1, the glycogen branching enzyme gene, in trans (biallelic). Echocardiogram 3/28 normal, EF 60%. Abdominal ultrasound 3/28 with normal liver and spleen.

Diagnosis: glycogen storage disease type IV (Andersen disease), neuromuscular presentation with exercise intolerance and episodic myoglobinuria. No evidence of liver or cardiac involvement at this time.

Genetics: autosomal recessive; his parents are obligate carriers. Siblings would each have had a 1 in 4 chance; he reports none. Genetic counseling offered; he will think about it.

Counseling given:
- Avoid all-out anaerobic exertion and heavy isometric lifting. Moderate walking, cycling at conversational pace are fine.
- Keep well hydrated, especially in heat.
- Dark urine with muscle pain, or any high fever with muscle stiffness, needs same-day medical evaluation and a CK.
- Please make sure any clinician starting new medicines knows his muscle condition.

Follow-up: yearly in this clinic with CK; echo and liver imaging every few years or sooner for symptoms.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Neuromuscular attending

documents.title: Results discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Calvin about the neuromuscular letter. He had already heard from them and understood the basics: genetic, from both parents, explains the cramps, heart and liver look fine. Added GSD IV to the problem list and an alert to the chart so anyone prescribing sees it. Asked him to tell his psychiatry team; I am also faxing the letter there with his permission. No questions otherwise.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update to primary care. Seen 6/6/2023.

Calvin is attending about twice a month. Persecutory ideas are less intense but not gone; he still hears whispering most days. He is going out with an old school friend now and then. Declines antipsychotic medication again; we respect this and keep the door open. Aware of his new diagnosis of glycogen storage disease type IV; noted in our record for future prescribing.

Dx: schizophrenia. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: continue therapy visits and case management.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, missed last year's.

Since last physical: schizophrenia diagnosed by community psychiatry in October, no medication by his choice, attends therapy and case management. GSD IV (neuromuscular form) confirmed in April by GBE1 testing; echo and liver ultrasound normal.

Today: no cramping episodes since spring, staying with walks and an easy stationary bike. No dark urine. Still hears whispering at times but says he can "tune it out." Not working, helping his father with yard work. Sleep better. Eating well.

Meds none. NKDA. No tobacco, no alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: weight 72.5 kg, back toward his usual. Vitals normal. Groomed, more spontaneous than last fall, affect still restricted. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen edge. Strength full. Skin clear.

PHQ-9 4.

A/P: 1) GSD IV: CK and liver tests today; yearly neuromuscular follow-up. 2) Schizophrenia: per psychiatry, stable, not on meds. 3) Health maintenance: flu in the fall, covid booster up to him, Td due 2031.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Calvin. CK is in the same range it has been, which for you is your normal resting level. Liver tests, kidney function, sodium and potassium are all normal. No changes.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Mother drove him. No acute illness. Declined covid vaccine today. Tolerated without issue.

events.reason: Hyperthermia and confusion after MDMA ingestion

documents.title: Emergency Department Record and Observation Summary
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT / OBSERVATION UNIT
Arrival 12/16/2023 01:20. Discharged from observation 12/18/2023 11:30.

HPI: 24-year-old man brought in by two friends from a concert. Per friends he swallowed "a small pill" in the evening, presumed MDMA. For hours afterward he was elated, chatty and full of energy, dancing nonstop and drinking bottle after bottle of water, saying he was overheating. Over the last hour or so he became anxious and muddled, prompting the friends to bring him in. History otherwise from chart and friends: schizophrenia, untreated; glycogen storage disease type IV (neuromuscular form). No medications. NKDA.

Exam on arrival: T 40.0 C, BP 150/90, HR 128, RR 26, SpO2 98% RA. Skin flushed and wet. Pupils dilated, reactive. Mild jaw clenching. Alert, restless, oriented to person only intermittently. Fine tremor; intermittent increased tone in the limbs, not sustained. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: Na 131 (mildly low). HCO3 17 with an elevated anion gap; metabolic acidosis. CK 14,600. Creatinine within normal limits. Urine drug screen negative for amphetamines, cocaine and opioids (standard immunoassay does not reliably detect MDMA).

Course: active cooling with ice packs and misting fan; lorazepam IV for agitation and tone; free water restricted, isotonic saline boluses then high-rate maintenance fluids for rhabdomyolysis given his muscle disease. Temperature normal by hour 4, mental status clear by morning. Sodium corrected gradually. Placed in observation for fluids and serial CK. CK 8,900 on the morning of 12/18 and falling, urine clear, eating and drinking, creatinine normal throughout.

Diagnoses: MDMA intoxication with hyperthermia; rhabdomyolysis treated with IV fluid resuscitation; mild hyponatremia; metabolic acidosis, resolved.

Disposition: home with mother. Push oral fluids, no exercise this week. Substance counseling given. PCP follow-up within the week with repeat CK and BMP. Return for dark urine, confusion, fever or decreased urine.
Allergies: NKDA.
ED attending / observation attending

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED and observation summary received this morning. Called pt. Home since yesterday, tired, legs a bit sore, urine light yellow. Drinking plenty. No fever, no confusion. Booked with PCP Thursday 12/21 for CK and BMP recheck. Told him to go back if urine darkens or he feels unwell.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the ED and observation stay 12/16 to 12/18 for MDMA intoxication with hyperthermia and rhabdomyolysis. Record reviewed: Na 131, HCO3 17, CK 14,600 on arrival, CK 8,900 at discharge.

He says it was the first time he has taken anything like that; a friend offered it at the show. Remembers little of the ED. Legs were sore for two days, now fine. Urine normal color. Drinking well. No fever. Mood "embarrassed." Still in care with psychiatry, still no meds.

Exam: well appearing, vitals normal, afebrile. No muscle tenderness, full strength. Mental status clear.

A/P:
1) Rhabdomyolysis after MDMA, in the setting of GSD IV: CK and BMP today; light activity only until CK is near his baseline.
2) MDMA intoxication: resolved. Talked plainly about how much more dangerous stimulants and overheating are for his muscles, and about how they can worsen psychosis. He says he won't use again. Will let psychiatry know (permission given).

Will message results.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calvin, your CK is down to 1,150 from 8,900 at discharge, so the muscle is settling. Sodium is back to normal at 139 and your kidneys are fine. Keep to walking for now. Let's recheck the CK in about three weeks; I put in the order, any weekday morning at our lab.

documents.title: CK recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CK 710, back in his usual range. Rhabdo resolved. Message sent to pt: fine to go back to his walking and easy bike routine.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, interval summary for primary care. Visit 2/6/2024.

We were sorry to hear of the December ED visit after MDMA. He tells us it was a one-time use; we talked about the effect of stimulants on psychosis. He has not used since.

Symptoms: voices most days, low volume; ongoing belief that his phone is tracked, less preoccupied by it. Some days he does not leave his room. Engaged with case manager, considering a part-time volunteer role.

Medication: he continues to decline an antipsychotic. Allergies: NKDA.
Dx: schizophrenia; history noted of GSD IV.
Plan: visits every 2 to 3 weeks.

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Annual Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Annual follow-up 3/19/2024. Glycogen storage disease type IV, neuromuscular form (biallelic GBE1).

Interval: one episode of rhabdomyolysis in December 2023 in the setting of MDMA intoxication and hyperthermia, treated with fluids, resolved. No exertional episodes otherwise; he keeps to walking and easy cycling.

Exam: strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes normal, no hepatomegaly.
CK today at his resting baseline.

Impression: stable. The December episode shows how hyperthermia and drug toxicity can tip him into significant muscle breakdown.
Recommendations unchanged: avoid maximal anaerobic effort, hydrate, avoid stimulants; any fever with rigidity or dark urine needs urgent evaluation with CK. Prescribers should weigh muscle toxicity of new medications. Return in one year.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Neuromuscular attending

documents.title: Exercise question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor. My case manager found me a cheap gym membership. Is it ok to use the machines? I don't want to end up in the hospital again.

documents.title: RE: Exercise question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question, and good that you asked. The treadmill, bike and elliptical at an easy to moderate pace are fine, where you can still talk while you go. Skip the heavy weights and anything all-out or sprint-style, and stop at the first sign of cramping. Bring water. If your urine turns dark after a workout, call us that day.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 24 y/o.

Problems: schizophrenia (community psychiatry, declines medication); GSD IV neuromuscular form (yearly neuromuscular follow-up, stable in March); rhabdomyolysis Dec 2023 after MDMA, resolved.

Interval: using the gym about three mornings a week, bike and treadmill only. No cramps, no dark urine. No substance use since December. Volunteering a few hours a week sorting donations. Voices are "background." Sleeping and eating fine.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: weight 74 kg. Vitals normal. Calm, organized, restricted affect. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no organomegaly. Full strength. Skin normal.

PHQ-9 3.

A/P: doing well on both fronts. CMP and CK today. Flu shot in the fall. Continue psychiatry and neuromuscular follow-up. Return one year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calvin, CK is at your usual level even with the gym routine, which is reassuring. Chemistry panel normal.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update to primary care. Visit 10/8/2024.

Over the past month his voices have become louder and more critical, and he stopped volunteering because he felt watched there. After many conversations he now agrees to try medication.

Started risperidone 1 mg by mouth twice daily. Reviewed side effects including stiffness, restlessness and the rare but serious reaction of fever with rigidity and confusion, especially relevant with his muscle disease; family told to seek emergency care for any of these. Baseline weight, BP and metabolic labs reviewed from primary care (August).

Dx: schizophrenia. Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: see in 2 weeks; case manager weekly.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 10/22/2024 16:40.

HPI: 24-year-old man with schizophrenia and glycogen storage disease type IV, seen here last December after MDMA ingestion. His parents bring him in because since yesterday he has been feverish, stiff and confused. About two weeks ago his psychiatrist started a new medicine; the family does not know its name. Pharmacy lookup by our staff shows risperidone 1 mg twice daily filled 10/8.

Exam: T 39.5 C, HR 110, BP 160/90, RR 22. Drenched in sweat. Lead-pipe rigidity of all four limbs. Confused, agitated, not following commands consistently. No clonus, pupils mid-size. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: WBC 15.0. CK 5,000. Sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate and creatinine normal. AST 92, ALT 61 (mildly elevated). Urine dark brown, large blood, no leukocyte esterase or nitrite, no WBCs.

Impression: neuroleptic malignant syndrome due to risperidone, in a patient with an underlying metabolic myopathy.

ED management: risperidone stopped; external cooling; IV normal saline; lorazepam IV. Critical care consulted.

Disposition: admitted to the medical ICU.
Allergies on arrival: NKDA. Added: risperidone (NMS).
ED attending

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, MEDICAL ICU AND MEDICINE SERVICE
Admitted 10/22/2024. Discharged 10/28/2024.

Principal diagnosis: neuroleptic malignant syndrome (risperidone).
Other: schizophrenia; glycogen storage disease type IV, neuromuscular form.

Course: Admitted to the ICU febrile, rigid and confused two weeks after starting risperidone. Antipsychotic stopped on arrival. Treated with cooling blankets, aggressive IV fluids to protect the kidneys, scheduled IV lorazepam, IV dantrolene for 2 days and bromocriptine by mouth, tapered off before discharge. Fever resolved by day 2 and rigidity eased over days 2 to 4; mental status back to baseline by day 4. CK peaked on day 1 and fell steadily, 680 on the day of discharge. Creatinine normal throughout. Moved to the floor on day 4. Psychiatry consult saw him in house: no antipsychotic for now; outpatient team to decide on any future trial, with at least several weeks' wait and a different agent only under close monitoring.

Discharge medications: none.
Allergies/intolerances: risperidone, neuroleptic malignant syndrome (new).

Follow-up: PCP within one week with CK and BMP; outpatient psychiatry within 2 weeks.
Instructions: avoid all antipsychotics and metoclopramide-type drugs until reviewed by psychiatry; return for fever, stiffness or confusion.
Attending hospitalist

documents.title: Mother calling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called to let us know Calvin was admitted to the ICU Tuesday night with a reaction to his new psychiatric medicine, fever and stiffness. She says he is more awake today and the fever is down. She will call when he is discharged. Records request sent to the hospital. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Will see him within a week of discharge.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record and discharge summary received today, attached. Called pt within 2 business days of discharge; mother also on the line. Home since 10/28. No fever, no stiffness, walking normally, urine clear, eating. No medications. Knows not to take any antipsychotic for now. Risperidone added to allergy list as NMS reaction. TCM visit Friday 11/1 with PCP, labs that day.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, with mother.

Admitted 10/22 to 10/28, medical ICU then floor, for neuroleptic malignant syndrome two weeks after starting risperidone 1 mg BID. ED: T 39.5, HR 110, BP 160/90, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion; WBC 15.0, CK 5,000, AST 92 and ALT 61, urine dark without infection. Treated with cooling, fluids, lorazepam, dantrolene and bromocriptine. CK 680 at discharge. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Now: feels "wiped out" but better daily. No fever. No stiffness. Urine normal. Eating. Sleep ok. Voices about where they were before the medicine. No SI.

Meds: none. Allergies: risperidone (NMS).

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Alert, oriented, conversant. No rigidity, no tremor, tone normal. Strength full. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P:
1) NMS, resolved clinically. CK and BMP today. Allergy list updated. Clear instructions to family: no antipsychotics or antiemetics like metoclopramide/prochlorperazine without psychiatry and me knowing.
2) Schizophrenia: psychiatry appointment 11/12. I will send them the summary.
3) GSD IV: muscle recovery; no gym for 2 weeks, then easy only.
4) Flu vaccine today.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called mother with today's results: CK 520, which is his usual resting level, and BMP normal. Muscles have recovered. Gym after two weeks, easy pace.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, letter to primary care. Visit 11/12/2024.

Seen after his ICU admission for NMS on risperidone. Physically recovered. Psychotic symptoms back to the pre-medication level: daily low-volume voices, persistent ideas of being monitored, no command content, no SI/HI. Understandably the family is frightened of medication now.

Plan: antipsychotics held for now. We will revisit in the coming months; any future trial would be a different agent, low dose, slow increase, with family watching for fever or stiffness and a low threshold for CK. Continue therapy every 2 weeks and case management.

Allergies: risperidone (NMS). Meds: none.
Dx: schizophrenia.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, interval letter. Visit 2/11/2025.

Off all antipsychotics since the NMS admission in October. Symptoms steady at his usual level: voices most days, monitoring beliefs, some withdrawal on bad days. Attends therapy reliably, back to volunteering one morning a week. No substance use. No SI/HI.

We discussed a future medication trial. He and his parents are not ready. We will keep talking.

Allergies: risperidone (NMS). Meds: none.

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Annual Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Visit 3/18/2025. GSD IV, neuromuscular form.

Interval: admitted in October 2024 with neuroleptic malignant syndrome on risperidone; CK 5,000 at presentation, recovered. No exertional episodes; exercises at a moderate pace three times a week.

Exam unchanged: full strength, normal reflexes, no organomegaly. CK today at baseline.

Comment: his myopathy may make the muscle injury of any future NMS worse and makes CK a less specific marker; a rise well above his baseline of roughly 500 to 700 is the meaningful signal. If psychiatry considers another antipsychotic, we would favor the lowest-risk option, slow titration and early CK checks for any fever or stiffness.

Plan: return in one year.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS). Meds: none.
Neuromuscular attending

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check-in after last fall's admission.

Doing about the same. Volunteering weekly, gym twice a week at an easy pace. No cramping, no dark urine. Psychiatry every two weeks, no medication. Voices daily, "manageable." Sleep fine. Appetite fine. No substances.

Meds none. Intolerance: risperidone (NMS).

Exam: vitals normal, weight stable. Calm, logical, restricted affect. Heart and lungs normal.

PHQ-9 5, no item 9.

A/P: schizophrenia per psychiatry; GSD IV stable per neuromuscular in March, CK baseline. Physical in August with labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 25 y/o.

Active: schizophrenia, off medication since the NMS in Oct 2024; GSD IV, neuromuscular form, stable. Intolerance: risperidone (NMS).

Interval: psychiatry raised trying a different medicine this fall; he is considering it. No new physical complaints. Gym easy pace, no cramps, no dark urine. No substances, no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: weight 73.5 kg. Vitals normal. Well groomed, organized speech, restricted affect. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Strength 5/5 throughout. Skin normal.

PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
- Labs today with a metabolic baseline in case psychiatry starts a medication: CBC with diff, CMP, lipids, A1c, CK.
- If a new antipsychotic is started, family knows: fever, stiffness or confusion means the ED the same day, and to tell them about the prior NMS and his muscle disease.
- Flu shot in October.
- Return in a year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Calvin. Everything from Tuesday is normal: blood counts, chemistry and liver tests, cholesterol and A1c. CK is in your usual range. I've copied the results to your psychiatry clinic.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Feeling well. Declined covid vaccine this year. No issues after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update to primary care. Visit 10/24/2025.

Over the past two months his voices and fears about being monitored have intensified and he stopped volunteering. He and his parents asked to try medication again.

After a long discussion of risks, including recurrence of NMS given the October 2024 episode on risperidone, we chose aripiprazole 5 mg daily, a partial agonist with a lower reported NMS risk, at a low starting dose. He plans to start Sunday 10/26 so a parent is home for the first days. Family instructed: check his temperature twice daily for two weeks; any fever, stiffness, sweating or confusion means the ED immediately, bringing this letter.

Allergies: risperidone (NMS). Meds: aripiprazole 5 mg daily (new).
Plan: phone check 10/29, visit 11/7.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 10/28/2025 19:50.

HPI: 25-year-old man with schizophrenia, GSD IV (neuromuscular) and NMS on risperidone in October 2024. Mother brought him in: for two days he has had a rising fever, worsening stiffness and confusion. He began a new psychiatric medication two days ago (aripiprazole 5 mg, first dose 10/26, per the psychiatry letter she brought). He cannot give any history himself.

Exam: T 39.5 C, HR 110, BP 160/90, RR 24. Profuse sweating. Severe rigidity in all four extremities. Confused, mumbling, not oriented. No clonus. Lungs clear.

Labs: WBC 15.0. CK 5,000. Potassium 5.2. Sodium 140. Creatinine 1.2.

Impression: recurrent neuroleptic malignant syndrome, now with aripiprazole.

Management: aripiprazole stopped; cooling; IV fluids; IV lorazepam; IV dantrolene started in the ED after critical care discussion.
Disposition: medical ICU.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS); aripiprazole added (NMS).
ED attending

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, MEDICAL ICU AND MEDICINE SERVICE
Admitted 10/28/2025. Discharged 11/7/2025.

Principal diagnosis: neuroleptic malignant syndrome, recurrent (aripiprazole); prior episode with risperidone 10/2024.
Other: schizophrenia; glycogen storage disease type IV, neuromuscular form.

Course: Presented febrile to 39.5 C, markedly rigid and confused two days after starting aripiprazole 5 mg. Aripiprazole stopped. ICU for 5 days: cooling, IV fluids titrated to urine output, IV lorazepam, IV dantrolene for 3 days, bromocriptine by mouth tapered over the following week. Potassium 5.2 on arrival corrected with fluids; creatinine 1.2 on arrival improved to 0.9. Rigidity slower to settle than last year; mental status at baseline by day 6. CK 590 on day of discharge. Moved to the floor on day 6, worked with physical therapy, walking independently.

Inpatient psychiatry consult: two NMS episodes with two different agents. Recommend no antipsychotic in the near term; outpatient psychiatry to weigh options, which may include clozapine with very slow titration and close monitoring, or ECT.

Discharge medications: none.
Allergies/intolerances: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (CK, BMP); outpatient psychiatry 11/18.
Attending hospitalist

documents.title: Mother calling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called: Calvin was admitted to the ICU last night, fever and rigidity again, two days after starting aripiprazole. She brought the psychiatry letter and they started treatment right away. She is upset; listened, answered what I could. Records request faxed. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called mother back briefly. Will see him after discharge. Aripiprazole will go on the intolerance list once records arrive.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary and ED record received, attached. Spoke with pt and mother. Home since Friday 11/7. No fever. Legs still a little stiff in the morning, loosening through the day; walking on his own. Urine clear. Eating. No medications. Aripiprazole added to allergy list (NMS). TCM visit Thursday 11/13.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit with mother.

Second NMS. Started aripiprazole 5 mg 10/26, ED 10/28 with T 39.5, HR 110, BP 160/90, rigid in all limbs, confused; WBC 15.0, CK 5,000, K 5.2, Na 140, Cr 1.2. ICU, cooling, fluids, lorazepam, dantrolene, bromocriptine. Discharged 11/7, CK 590, Cr 0.9. Records reviewed.

Now: morning stiffness gone since the weekend. No fever. Tired. Urine normal. Mood low about "another hospital"; no SI. Voices as before.

Meds none. Intolerances: risperidone and aripiprazole, both NMS.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Alert, oriented. Tone normal, no rigidity, no tremor. Strength 5/5. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1) NMS x2, resolved. CK and BMP today.
2) Schizophrenia: psychiatry 11/18. The hospital consult mentioned clozapine or ECT as options. I'll speak with his psychiatrist; we can draw any monitoring labs here to save him the trip.
3) GSD IV: no gym for two weeks.
4) Flu vaccine already given in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calvin, CK came back at 600, your usual level, and the kidney tests and potassium are normal. Your muscles have recovered from the episode.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, letter to primary care. Visit 12/2/2025 (also seen 11/18).

Two episodes of NMS: risperidone (10/2024) and aripiprazole (10/2025). He has persistent positive symptoms and has lost the gains of the past year. He and his parents want treatment but are frightened.

Options reviewed: ECT, or clozapine started at a very low dose with a slow climb, after an interval of at least 8 weeks from the last episode. They prefer clozapine.

Plan:
- Clozapine to start mid-January at 12.5 mg at bedtime, increase by small steps every few days as tolerated.
- Baseline CBC with ANC and CK the week before, then weekly CBC with ANC and CK for 6 months, then every 2 weeks. Primary care has kindly offered to draw these; we will send the standing order request.
- Temperature twice daily for the first month; any fever, stiffness or confusion: ED.
- Constipation, drooling and sedation reviewed.

Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS). Meds: none.

documents.title: Call with psychiatrist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his psychiatrist. Agree with the clozapine plan. Standing order entered here: CBC with diff (ANC) and CK, baseline the week of 1/12, then weekly for 26 weeks, then every 2 weeks. Results auto-faxed to psychiatry. ANC thresholds per their protocol; they own dosing. CK: we agreed that anything above about 1,500, or any fever, gets a same-day call between us. Lab and front desk notified.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Baseline before clozapine. CBC with diff and CK resulted, ANC normal, CK at his usual level. Faxed to psychiatry per standing order. Confirmation received.

medications.sig: Take 1/2 tablet (12.5 mg) by mouth at bedtime; increase as directed by psychiatry

documents.title: Psychiatry Letter: Clozapine Started
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, letter to primary care. Visit 1/13/2026.

Baseline ANC from your lab 1/12 normal; CK at his baseline. Clozapine started tonight at 12.5 mg at bedtime. Increase by 12.5 to 25 mg every 3 to 4 days if tolerated, aiming for about 100 mg at bedtime by late February, then reassess. Temperature log twice daily. Weekly CBC with ANC and CK through your standing order; thank you.

Symptoms: daily voices, monitoring beliefs, poor sleep. No SI/HI.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).
Meds: clozapine as above (dispensed through the specialty pharmacy).

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy called for the most recent ANC before dispensing clozapine. Read back 1/12 result and faxed the report. They will release the first fill today.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Week 1 on clozapine. ANC normal, CK at baseline. Pt reports no fever on his log. Faxed to psychiatry.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Week 3. ANC normal. CK at baseline. Faxed.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Week 6. Counts and CK normal for him. Pt mentions he is now at 100 mg at night. Faxed to psychiatry.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update. Visit 2/24/2026.

Titration went smoothly. Now clozapine 100 mg at bedtime (one 100 mg tablet). No fever on his log, no stiffness. Some morning grogginess and more saliva at night; using a towel on the pillow. Bowels regular. Voices a little quieter; sleeping through the night for the first time in months.

ANC normal every week, CK flat at his baseline. Thank you for the draws.
Plan: hold at 100 mg for 6 weeks, then consider 150 mg.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in eight weeks into clozapine (psychiatry managing; 100 mg at bedtime since late February).

He says he feels "less crowded in my head." Sleeping well, a bit slow in the mornings. Drools on the pillow some nights. Bowels every day or two, no straining. No fever, no stiffness, temperature log normal. Eating more; weight up about 1.5 kg. Back at the gym twice a week, easy pace, no cramps.

Meds: clozapine 100 mg qhs (psychiatry). Intolerances: risperidone, aripiprazole (both NMS).

Exam: weight 75 kg. BP, HR normal, afebrile. Brighter, better eye contact, organized. No rigidity, no tremor. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, bowel sounds normal, nontender.

PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
1) Schizophrenia on clozapine: tolerating. Weekly CBC/ANC and CK continue; drawn today with a BMP. Watch weight; A1c and lipids at his physical.
2) Bowel habits fine for now; he knows to call if he goes 3 days without a movement, a known clozapine problem.
3) GSD IV: stable, neuromuscular next week.
Return in August for the physical.

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Annual Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC
Visit 3/17/2026. GSD IV, neuromuscular form.

Interval: second NMS in October 2025 on aripiprazole, recovered. Started clozapine in January under psychiatry with weekly CK through primary care, all at his baseline.

Exam: full strength throughout, reflexes normal, no organomegaly, no rigidity.

Impression: stable myopathy. No new muscle concerns with clozapine so far.
Recommendations: continue CK monitoring with the ANC draws; hydrate; moderate exercise only. Echo and liver ultrasound due next year (3 years from 2023). Return in one year.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS). Meds: clozapine 100 mg at bedtime.
Neuromuscular attending

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ANC normal, CK unchanged. Faxed.

medications.sig: Take 1 and 1/2 tablets (150 mg) by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update. Visit 4/7/2026.

Six weeks at 100 mg with partial response: voices quieter, still present daily; less guarded. Labs normal throughout. No fever or stiffness ever on clozapine.

Increasing to 150 mg at bedtime (one and a half 100 mg tablets) from tonight. Temperature log again for two weeks after the increase.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ANC normal, CK at baseline. Faxed. Pt asks if the weekly draws will ever end; told him the schedule is set by psychiatry and usually spaces out after six months.

documents.title: Blood draws
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. Do I still have to come every Tuesday for blood? My psychiatrist said it might get less often. Also can I go at 7:30 instead of 8 so I can get to my volunteer shift?

documents.title: RE: Blood draws
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Calvin. Weekly draws continue until mid-July (26 weeks), then every two weeks; that comes from psychiatry and we follow their order. The lab opens at 7:30, so that works, just walk in.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ANC and CK normal. Faxed.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update. Visit 6/16/2026.

On clozapine 150 mg at bedtime for ten weeks. Best stretch in years per patient and parents: voices occasional and quiet, no longer convinced his phone is monitored, back at volunteering two mornings a week and talking about a community college class in the spring. Night drooling persists, tolerable. Bowels regular. Weight up a few pounds.

ANC normal on every draw; CK steady at his baseline.
Plan: stay at 150 mg. Labs every 2 weeks after the 26-week mark in mid-July. Next visit in 8 weeks.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).

documents.title: Lab schedule change
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Calvin, a heads-up: after your draw on Tuesday 7/14 your clozapine labs go to every other week. Next one after that is 7/28. Your physical is 8/14 and we'll do that week's draw at the visit.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Last weekly draw (26 weeks). ANC normal throughout. Moving to every 2 weeks per standing order. Faxed.

documents.title: Clozapine monitoring labs
documents.author: MA
documents.body: First every-2-week draw. ANC normal, CK at baseline. Faxed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 26 y/o.

Problems: schizophrenia, on clozapine 150 mg qhs since April (psychiatry), good response; GSD IV, neuromuscular form, stable (neuromuscular 3/2026); NMS x2 (risperidone 10/2024, aripiprazole 10/2025), resolved.
Intolerances: risperidone, aripiprazole (NMS).

Interval: "the most normal year in a while." Volunteering two mornings a week, enrolled for a community college class in January. Voices rare and quiet. Sleeping 9 hours. Still drools at night. Bowels daily. Gym twice a week, easy pace, no cramps or dark urine. No substances, no tobacco, no alcohol. Labs every 2 weeks now, all fine.

Exam: weight 77 kg, up about 3.5 kg over the year on clozapine. Vitals normal, afebrile. Well groomed, bright, good eye contact, organized speech. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Strength 5/5, tone normal, no tremor. Skin normal.

PHQ-9 2.

A/P:
1) Schizophrenia on clozapine: CBC/ANC and CK today as this cycle's monitoring draw; standing order renewed for every 2 weeks. Metabolic check: CMP, lipids, A1c today.
2) Weight gain on clozapine: modest. Talked about portions and keeping up the gym; recheck at next visit.
3) GSD IV: stable.
4) Health maintenance: flu shot in the fall; covid vaccine offered, he will think about it. Td due 2031.
Return in 6 months, or sooner for anything.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Calvin, your labs from Friday are all good. White count and neutrophils normal, so the clozapine monitoring is fine; I've faxed them to psychiatry. Sugar (A1c), cholesterol, kidney and liver tests are normal. CK is in your usual range. Next blood draw in two weeks.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community behavioral health clinic, update. Visit 8/18/2026.

Stable on clozapine 150 mg at bedtime. Occasional quiet voices, no persecutory ideas voiced today. Plans to start a community college class in January; we support it. Labs every two weeks through primary care, all normal, including your 8/14 panel.

Plan: continue 150 mg. Next visit in 8 weeks.
Allergies: risperidone (NMS), aripiprazole (NMS).
